To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reviewers should provide a critical analysis of a manuscript’s strengths and areas of improvements, that reviewers should speak to the manuscript’s value to the literature, and that reviewers should be developed through hands-on experience and exposure to good reviews.

the following characteristics of reviews enhance manuscript quality: includes a critical review of the manuscript, includes both strengths and areas for improvement, and speaks to the utility of the manuscript in the literature.

the characteristics of reviews that were rated required or highly helpful in enhancing manuscript and editorial quality by all respondents were: includes a critical analyses of the manuscript, includes feedback that contains strengths and areas of improvements, speaks to the manuscript's utility in the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, “How do we develop good peer reviewers and how can we enhance the quality of peer reviews?”
the question: How can we help new reviewers develop into good reviewers, and how can we help good reviewers develop into better reviewers?
the development of a model of the relationship between the quality of a manuscript and the quality of the peer review process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a well-trained reviewer is one who has a good grasp of the topic and can provide an objective, critical, and insightful review of a manuscript.
a good reviewer provides a critical analysis of a manuscript and includes feedback that contains strengths and areas of improvements.
the editors and reviewers are the key to the manuscript quality and editorial decision making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peer review and reviewer training are essential to the success of scholarly publishing.
the peer review process can be improved through the development of reviewers and the development of a reviewer’s knowledge base, skills, and critical thinking.
the peer review process is a critical element in the publication process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peer review process is a critical part of manuscript evaluation and that reviewers play a key role in this process.
peer review is a critical component of scholarly publication and should be a key component in faculty development.
editors, reviewers, and authors should work together to improve the quality of the manuscript, and that editors should be open to feedback and constructive criticism from reviewers.
